newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anaconda nudges Murrin Murrin resource up.
newsitem.headline: Anaconda nudges Murrin Murrin resource up.

text.p: Nickel project developer Anaconda Nickel Ltd announced on Thursday a slight increase in the total resource estimate at its Murrin Murrin nickel/cobalt project in Western Australia.

Anaconda said the total updated resource, calculated from the results of infill drilling in September and October 1996, had increased to 128.4 million tonnes at 1.01 percent nickel and 0.064 percent cobalt from the feasibility study's resource estimate of 125.2 million tonnes at 1.02 percent nickel and 0.065 percent cobalt.
Anaconda Technical Director Geoff Motteram said the significant change was in the Measured Resource, which was updated to 87.7 million tonnes at 1.03 percent nickel and 0.065 percent cobalt.
The Measured Resource represented 68 percent of the Total Resource.
"The real change is that the amount of Measured Resource has increased quite significantly," Motteram said.
"It's about double the amount in the feasibility study," he said.
The Measured Resource was expected to rise from that given in the feasibility study as infill drilling was done, but this confirmed the substantial size of the project, he said.
"The confidence on the ore resource has increased very substantially," Motteram said.
The A$900 million Murrin Murrin project is located east of the outback town of Leonora in Western Australia.
Murrin Murrin is scheduled to come on stream at the end of 1998 and to reach production of 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt in that year.
Glencore International AG of Switzerland, which has a 40 percent stake in Murrin Murrin and a 19.0 percent stake in Anaconda Nickel, has exclusive rights to sell the cobalt and nickel.
Anaconda has plans to expand annual production to 75,000 tonnes of nickel and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt once the base plant is commissioned.
Anaconda's shares were steady at A$3.68 at 3.15 p.m. (0515 GMT).
